paragraphs.source_en: Although he sided with religious rebels in the Habsburg Empire, Suleiman I still faced competition for his spiritual role and the source of the dynasty’s legitimacy within his own empire. He faced large-scale, violent rebellions in central Anatolia from deviant dervishes, such as that led in 1527 by the Sufi Kalender Celebi, heir of Hajji Bektas and leader of his shrine in central Anatolia, whose supporters destroyed the first army sent to defeat it. His devotees raised their banners and beat their kettledrums and blew their horns in support. A Bektasi poet proclaimed, ‘O Ottoman! This world will not be left to you. Do not assume that Son of the Shah will not avenge this blood on you’.” Kalender Celebi was killed by Ottoman forces, ending his rebellion, and the shrine of Hajji Bektas was closed for nearly three decades.
